pageCache.text:
Welcome to Eynsham Community Primary School
Headteacher's welcome
Headteacher's welcome
Welcome to Eynsham Community Primary School
Mrs Nicola Edwards Headteacher
A vibrant two-form entry primary school serving the village of Eynsham. We are proud to be a community school, putting ourselves at the centre of the village community and encouraging every child to 'Soar to Success'.
Our school strives for excellence in academic and pastoral provision, placing high quality, engaging texts at the centre of our rich curriculum. We promote the British Values of: Democracy, Rule of Law, Individual Liberty and Mutual Respect and Tolerance for those of different faiths and beliefs. Being 'Ready, Respectful and Responsible' is at the heart of everything we do. We believe that an outstanding education is built from positive relationships with both children and parents. We recognise children as unique individuals with talents and needs that are nurtured through inclusive classrooms; where they can flourish and reach their full potential.
Our school is part of the EPA Trust which includes eight other primary schools, an all-through school (Heyford Park) and a local secondary school (Bartholomew School). Our children benefit from opportunities, particularly in sport, across the trust, as well as from the CPD provided for our staff.
Our website provides an insight to the outstanding provision that takes place in our school. It also includes all the introductory and statutory information you need, as well as showcasing just some of the things that make our school so special.
Please note, copies of the documents on this website can be made available from the school office.
Our Privacy Notice can be read here (Located on the School Policies & Procedures page). Whilst we do not use cookies on this school website, third party cookies may be used by some analytical and statistical plugins installed on the website to enhance their service. Full details of cookie usage can be found in our website Cookies Policy

Welcome to Eynsham Community Primary School
Owlets Wraparound Care
Owlets Wraparound Care
We understand that families often need childcare beyond the usual school day, which is why we offer our Owlets Wraparound Care for children aged 2–4 years.
Owlets provides a familiar, safe and nurturing environment for children before and after their nursery sessions. Children are cared for by our Early Years team, allowing them to enjoy a seamless transition between their nursery day and wraparound care.
Our Breakfast Club provides a calm and welcoming start to the day, while our after-school sessions give children the opportunity to relax, play and enjoy a range of age-appropriate activities at the end of their nursery day.
Owlets sessions can be booked alongside your child's regular nursery sessions, helping families to create a childcare pattern that works for them.
For further information about session times, availability, fees and booking Owlets, please contact the nursery admin team at nursery@eynsham.oxon.sch.uk or call 01865 881294.

Welcome to Eynsham Community Primary School
Governors
Governors at Eynsham Community Primary School
The Governors work closely with Mrs Bayliss (Executive Headteacher), Mrs Edwards (Head of School) and staff at Eynsham Community Primary School and form the Local Governing Board (LGB) for the school. Eynsham Community Primary School is part of the Eynsham Partnership Academy Trust and the EPA scheme of delegation https://www.epa-mat.org/schemes-of-delegation/ sets out the roles, structure and responsibilities of the LGB. Please also see statutory information below.
The Governors are responsible for:
The LGB was set up in January 2020 and replaced the Rapid Improvement Board which the EPA had set up as a small group to work intensively with the headteacher and senior team to move the school out of the Ofsted ‘Requires Improvement’ category. Following the successful Ofsted inspection in autumn 2019, which categorised the school as ‘Good’, the RIB was renamed the LGB and is gradually expanding its membership to fully reflect the school’s community.
Governors are appointed from various sectors of the school’s community: parents/carers, staff, others who have skills and experience in education and leadership, and people working in the local community.
Meeting dates for the academic year 2025-2026 are as follows:

Governor Members
Peter Leonard - Chair of Governors
Peter has been a teacher, deputy headteacher and head of school in primary education. He has also been a Governor and Chair of Governors for local primary schools, Chair of a small Multi Academy Trust and trustee and Chair of Trustees for various charities. Peter is passionate about the importance of emotional health for everyone and is keen to see both greater awareness of and a framework of support for people to improve their emotional health and relationships. Peter is Chief Executive of The Centre for Emotional Health.
Lisa Podbery - Co-opted Governor
Lisa has worked at the School for the past 21 years in the admin office and for the last 9 years as School Manager. Her role is to manage the finance, support services, admin and premises teams and to provide a back up to the Headteacher.
Annie Billington - Staff Governor
Annie Billington has worked in the school for 7 years and her current role is a Higher Level Teaching Assistant. She also is the Attendance Officer.
Nicola Wilson - Academy Governor
Nic Wilson was formerly the Committee Chair and a Designated Safeguarding Lead at Eynsham Pre-school (now our Cygnets class). She's a Head of Acquisition at Oxford Univeristy Press, and she works with clinicians and academics across several medical areas, including Public Health and Paediatric Care. Nic has two children at the school.
Victoria Clark - Vice Chair
Victoria has worked in education for 16 years as an English Teacher across 2 Oxfordshire Secondary Schools, including being Head of English for 6 years. She has a wealth of Pastoral experience, most recently as a Head of Upper School leading on Raising Standards in Behaviour for Learning. Victoria is an Eynsham resident and has 3 children currently educated at the school.
Marion Everist - Parent Governor
Marion has worked in education for over 20 years, initially as a teacher and now as an Educational Psychologist. Marion lives in Eynsham and has two children, one at Eynsham Community Primary School and one at Bartholomew School.
Joanna Gill - Parent Governor
Jo is a parent governor with 2 children at the school. She works as a clinical psychologist in an NHS child and adolescent mental health service, and in post-graduate education at Oxford University.
Roger Cabera - Parent Governor
Roger has a background in business, where he has held roles in strategy, operations, finance and talent development. He lives in Eynsham, and is a parent of a child currently at Eynsham Primary.
Martin Willis - Parent Governor
Martin works for a consultancy firm specialising in pensions and is familiar with risk management and finance. He enjoys helping with the under 9's football team in the village and sits on the residents committee for the recent Abbey Green development.
Claire Bunyan - Parent Governor
Claire has 2 children at the school and works as a Senior Reserach Fellow in Cultural Anthropology. She specialises in securing funding for high value projects with complex budgets and timescales.
Lucy Dickinson - Clerk to the Governors
Lucy has joined as Clerk to the Governors. Currently self-employed as a governance professional, as well as doing freelance environmental, educational and publishing-related consultancy. Lucy has an academic background in chemistry, with several years’ experience in science publishing, and grants administration. She is also clerk for three other schools and a governor at Bartholomew School, as well as leading the EPA advisory board on climate and biodiversity.
Communication with the Governors
The Board will continue to keep all parents and carers regularly informed of the progress ECPS is making through the governor's and school’s newsletters and website.
Clerk to the Governors can be contacted at governor@eynshamapps.co.uk​​​​

Welcome to Eynsham Community Primary School
Holiday Clubs at our school
Holiday Clubs at our school
The Holiday Activities and Food (HAF) programme offers free holiday club places during the Winter, Easter and Summer school holidays. Places are available for children eligible for benefits‑related Free School Meals (FSM), and for a limited number of vulnerable children referred by schools, family support workers, foodbanks or social workers. Bookings for the summer programme will open on, or soon after, 9 June. Sessions will run on selected days between 18 July and 31 August. Parents booking before 1 July can book up to 8 sessions per eligible child.
After this date, they can book up to 16 sessions. See http://www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/hafinformation for details. Eligibility will be checked during the booking process and no voucher is required.
To make a booking please copy and paste this link https://eequ.org/hafoxfordshire

Welcome to Eynsham Community Primary School
Early Years Information
Early Years Information
A very warm welcome to Eynsham Nursery, where we provide a nurturing, happy and enriching environment in which our youngest children can learn, explore and grow.
We believe that the Early Years are some of the most important years in a child’s education, laying the foundations for future learning and development. Our dedicated and experienced Early Years team, overseen by a qualified teacher, work together to provide high-quality learning experiences that support each child’s individual needs and development, while ensuring that every child feels happy, safe and valued.
Through a wealth of stimulating, engaging and hands-on experiences, we encourage children to be curious, develop their independence, build confidence and discover the joy of learning through play and exploration.
As part of Eynsham Community Primary School, our nursery children are very much part of the wider school community. They benefit from the opportunities, facilities and experiences that being part of a primary school brings, while enjoying an Early Years environment carefully designed around their age and stage of development.
We are incredibly proud of our Early Years provision and the caring, welcoming environment we have created. We look forward to working in partnership with our families to give every child the very best start to their journey at Eynsham.
Early Years Fundung Information
There are a number of funded childcare options available to families, and you may be entitled to receive help towards the cost of your child’s nursery education.
All children aged 3 and 4 years old are entitled to 15 hours of funded early education each week, from the term following their third birthday. Eligible working families may be entitled to up to 30 hours of funded childcare per week.
Some families may also be eligible for funded early education for their child from an earlier age, depending on their individual circumstances.
As eligibility and funding arrangements can vary, we recommend visiting the Oxfordshire County Council website, where you can find the most up-to-date information about the different funding options, eligibility criteria and how to apply.
You can find information on available funding at:
Governement Early Years Funding Help
Oxfordshire County Council - Free early education for eligible working families
Tax-Free Childcare
We accept Tax-Free Childcare payments, which can help eligible working families with the cost of nursery and wraparound childcare.
For every £8 you pay into your online childcare account, the Government adds £2, meaning you could receive up to £2,000 per child, per year towards your childcare costs.
Tax-Free Childcare can be used towards eligible childcare costs that are not covered by your funded hours, including additional nursery sessions and eligible wraparound care.
Eligibility depends on your individual circumstances, including your child's age, your employment and your income. Parents apply for and manage Tax-Free Childcare through their Government childcare account.
For full eligibility information and to apply, please visit the GOV.UK Tax-Free Childcare service.
Find out more about Tax-Free Childcare
If you are unsure which funding may apply to your child, please contact the school office and we will be happy to help.
Forms and Information
As part of our commitment to sustainability and reducing our environmental impact, we aim to use electronic communication and online forms wherever possible. This helps us reduce paper usage, streamline our administration processes and ensure information is received securely and efficiently.
